RIGHTS: the instrument is Bartholomew & Horowitz's (1991) Relationship Questionnaire (four prototype paragraphs A-D, as printed in the W2 and W3 questionnaires). The originator's own page, Kim Bartholomew's SFU lab 'Adult Attachment Research Materials > Frequently asked questions' (http://members.psyc.sfu.ca/labs/kim_bartholomew/attachment/frequently_asked_questions; live host does not resolve today, read from Wayback snapshot 20200524202206, raw id_ capture sha256 713ae49ca7a1d3a8630ab2b1b9465df6811d57d32db2aa5186fc0e45cb7cb236, cached at itemtext/.cache/c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_rq/sfu_faq_wayback20200524.html), answers 'Do I need permission to use the RQ, RSQ, and/or Social Networks Questionnaire in my research?' with 'No, these measures are in the public domain. Therefore, you are welcome to use any of these questionnaires without charge in your research.' and then lists Exceptions, including: "Commercial use: You cannot use these measures for commercial purposes." Under the irw#1945 test a non-commercial restriction RESERVES A RIGHT -> block; IRW redistributes, so the holder's reservation reaches downstream users IRW cannot condition. A public-domain statement beside an NC clause does not override it (TIMSS 2003 rule), and the originator's page governs over the study's CC BY 4.0 deposit (DSES/HEXACO rulings; register precedents DIENER-NC, MEQ). The same FAQ's 'Clinical use: These measures were developed for research purposes only and are not appropriate for use in individual assessments' is a fitness disclaimer and does not block on its own. Tension recorded for Ben: the register's AUDIT row (2026-09-19) shipped an NC clause on 'IRW is non-commercial'; round practice since (MEQ, DIENER-NC, IRI, goyal stance) blocks NC, and the RQ page frames it as a 'You cannot' prohibition, so this round blocks and escalates rather than shipping.
